mcat_description.short: Portable Shelters are relocatable, prefabricated enclosures made from steel, FRP, aluminium, or PUF panel systems, designed for quick on-site assembly and temporary or semi-permanent use across industrial, agricultural, and infrastructure applications.
mcat_description.long: Portable Shelters are modular, pre-engineered structures manufactured off-site in controlled factory environments and transported to site for rapid installation, offering flexible and cost-effective protection for workers, equipment, vehicles, and agricultural produce. They are constructed using a variety of frame materials — mild steel (MS), galvanised iron (GI), aluminium, or FRP — combined with wall and roof panels such as PUF sandwich panels, GRP sheets, colour-coated steel sheets, or polycarbonate. In the Indian B2B market, these shelters serve a wide range of applications including construction site worker accommodation, equipment and storage protection, telecom BTS enclosures, agricultural rain shelters, vehicle parking canopies, military field shelters, and emergency/disaster relief structures. Key buyer decision factors include frame material, panel type and insulation rating, structural dimensions, weatherproofing, lifespan, and ease of assembly and relocation.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'Portable Shelters' and 'Prefabricated Shelters' are used interchangeably to describe relocatable, factory-built enclosures spanning a wide range of applications — from construction site worker accommodation and industrial equipment protection to telecom BTS enclosures, agricultural rain shelters, and military field shelters. The dominant construction materials are mild steel (MS) frames with PUF sandwich panels, GRP/FRP sheets, or colour-coated galvanised steel sheets; aluminium-frame variants are used for lighter vehicle canopy applications. Key manufacturing hubs in India include Faridabad (Haryana), Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Gurugram (Haryana), and Hyderabad (Telangana), with pan-India supply capability. Structural steel components in these shelters are governed by IS 800 (general construction in steel) and IS 875 (code of practice for design loads), while PUF panel insulation performance is a key differentiator for telecom and cold-chain applications. The telecom BTS shelter sub-segment is a distinct and technically specialised niche — sealed, insulated PUF panel cabins protecting telecom equipment from moisture, dust, and temperature extremes — with separate buyer profiles (telecom operators, tower companies) from the general industrial shelter segment. Agricultural rain shelters (retractable or fixed canopy over crops) represent a growing sub-segment driven by horticulture and protected cultivation demand in India. Sellers quote predominantly per square foot for custom-dimension structures and per piece for standard-size cabins.
